    Jordan blocks #

    The n × n Jordan block J_n(μ) with eigenvalue μ (jordanMatrix), acting on kⁿ by (J x)_i = μ x_i + x_{i+1} (jordan_apply). We prove:

    • J_n(μ) admits no nontrivial commuting idempotent (idemIndec_jordan);
    • J_n(μ) and J_n(μ') are not similar for μ ≠ μ' (eq_of_jordan_conj);
    • over an algebraically closed field, an automorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional space without nontrivial commuting idempotents is similar to a single Jordan block (exists_jordan): Fitting's decomposition makes it unipotent up to a scalar, and a cyclic vector of the nilpotent part has an invariant complement.

                Jordan normal form of an indecomposable automorphism. Over an algebraically closed field, an automorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional space without nontrivial commuting idempotents is similar to a single Jordan block J_n(μ), μ ≠ 0.
